title: adaptive-batcher-fairness-timeouts-and-backoff-tuning
author: Evan Cho
description:
Motivation: production traffic showed occasional tail-latency spikes when low-priority streams starved due to continuous batching favoring high-throughput prefixes. This PR introduces a tunable adaptive batching scheduler layer that enforces per-priority fairness, introduces starvation prevention timeouts, and adds a cooperative backoff mechanism to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Summary of changes (single-line description of each logical piece):
- scheduler/adaptive_batcher.cc/.h: new AdaptiveBatcher that maintains multiple queues (hot, warm, cold) per model shard, exposes tunable parameters: max_queue_delay_ms, fairness_window_ms, per_priority_max_batch_size, cooperative_backoff_factor. Implements deadline-based flushing when a request has been queued longer than max_queue_delay_ms to eliminate unbounded waiting.
- runtime/batcher_config.yaml: default profile with conservative timeouts and per-tenant overrides; documented knobs.
- serving/kv_cache/eviction_policy.cc: small change to ensure KV cache hits increment priority score for recently used streams so useful cached prefixes aren't repeatedly deprioritized.
- metrics/metrics_registry.cc: new histograms and counters (scheduler.queue_wait_ms, scheduler.starvation_events, scheduler.backoff_invocations) and associated console dashboard panel.
- tests/scheduler_test.cc: unit tests for fairness windowing and timeout-triggered flushes.
- benchmarks/benchmark_adaptive_batcher.py: synthetic benchmark harness used to measure throughput/latency tradeoffs under mixed-priority workloads.

Description and rationale:
Continuous batching is effective at reducing per-token cost, but in practice it creates priority inversion where aggressive streams with long prefixes monopolize batch construction. We observed two common failure modes: (1) small, latency-sensitive requests were repeatedly deferred leading to SLO violations; (2) cold tenants never accrued enough batching credit and experienced starvation under load. The AdaptiveBatcher addresses both by:
  * Enforcing fairness windows that limit how long a single priority class may dominate consecutive batch flushes;
  * Applying a starvation timeout that force-flushes queued work if it has waited longer than max_queue_delay_ms;
  * Using a cooperative backoff factor on streams that repeatedly cause oversized batches and push other priorities out, which temporarily reduces their maximum allowed sub-batch size.

Benchmark results (synthetic mixed workload, N=1000 requests/min, 20% high-throughput long-prefix streams, 80% low-latency short requests):
  * Baseline (old scheduler): median latency 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 730ms, throughput 98% of capacity; 1.6 starvation_events/min.
  * AdaptiveBatcher (defaults): median latency 36ms, p95 85ms, p99 160ms, throughput 95% of capacity; 0.05 starvation_events/min.
  * Aggressive timeout config (max_queue_delay_ms=5): p99 120ms, throughput 92% capacity — good for strict SLOs.

Staging canary plan: rollout as follows to minimize risk:
  1) Deploy AdaptiveBatcher behind a runtime flag.
  2) Canary 10% of requests for 24h using canary config with conservative timeouts and monitoring.
  3) If metrics (error rate, p99 latency, starvation_events) are stable, increase to 50% then 100%.

Testing and CI notes:
  - Added unit tests covering fairness window and timeout-triggered flush behavior.
  - Added an end-to-end synthetic benchmark that runs under our perf-canary harness to compare p99 under mixed loads.
  - CI initially failed lint (clang-format) and a missing include; fixed in second commit. All checks now pass: unit, integration, benchmark smoke.

Backward compatibility and rollout considerations:
  - Config defaults are intentionally conservative to avoid performance cliffs.
  - New metrics and runtime flags allow gradual tuning without restarts.
  - KV cache change is additive and only nudges priority accounting; no state migration required.

Related work and tickets: ENG-9044 (scheduler fairness investigation) and ENG-9112 (starvation incident RCA). References to internal notes: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-9044 and the incident writeup pinned in the ticket.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of AdaptiveBatcher and config knobs
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboard panels
- [x] Documentation for ops runbook and default config
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented in PR description

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness in the deadline/timeout math and the coop-backoff scheduler loop. I intentionally kept the per-shard queue data structures simple; if reviewers prefer we can introduce lock-free ring buffers in a follow-up to further reduce contention.

release_notes: Improved continuous batching scheduler: added per-priority fairness windows, starvation prevention timeouts, and cooperative backoff. New metrics: scheduler.queue_wait_ms, scheduler.starvation_events. Default configs conservative; configurable per-tenant.
additional_notes: This PR is intended to be low-risk with config-driven behavior. Ops should watch scheduler.starvation_events and p99 tail latency in the first 48h after canary. If unexpected regressions occur, the runtime flag can be toggled to revert to the previous scheduler.
